correctness.rationale: The rectangle Fourier factor is locally invertible after recovering a from I(0); the even derivatives give the six-distance power sums. The expansions in RESULT.md:61–75 give exactly the stated cubic. With Q>0 and W<P−2√Q one has P>E/3 and D(P)=F−8EP+12P²=(P−W)²−4Q>0. At fixed E,F, D increases to the right of E/3 and is negative at E/3 by 4E²−3F=(P−W)²+12Q. All admissible roots are therefore in one strictly increasing branch of the cubic. Recovery of U,V and of the inner midpoint's absolute displacement removes all ambiguities except reflection. I checked the frozen fourth-order collision: E=53 and F=3437 in both cases, the alternate squared-radius discriminant is 5749804/10000 with square root in (23.9,24), giving the stated strict gap margins at a=1/4, and P differs. Odd derivatives vanish. Independent verification also follows by the symmetric-pair-sum reduction below; no sampling or uploaded execution was needed.
